reframing_when: The question is framed entirely from the inside view — the specific case, the vivid narrative, the founders' passion — without anchoring to the outside view of what historically happens in the reference class.
The question asks 'will our plan work?' without first asking 'what is the historical success rate for plans like ours?' — base-rate neglect is shaping the inquiry.
The question treats the current case as unique when a credible reference class exists that would set a very different expectation for the outcome.
The question focuses on the mean or expected outcome without asking about the distribution — particularly the tail outcomes one or two standard deviations from the base case.
reframing_move: Anchor to the outside view: instead of asking about your specific case, ask 'what happens historically when companies/teams/projects like ours attempt this?' — the reference class forecasting reframe replaces inherited narrative with empirical prior.
curation_note: Base rates operates on question framing by replacing the inside view (which shapes the question's assumptions) with the outside view (which challenges them). The source is explicit: 'accuracy lives at the intersection between the inside view and the outside view' — the reframing move is to bring the outside view into a question that is stuck in the inside view.

reframing_when.note: All four activations grounded: inside vs outside view (core principle), base-rate neglect in planning (project management example), uniqueness assumption vs reference class (venture capital example), and tail outcome blindness (financial advising example).

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Borrowed premise: the question inherits assumptions from the inside view. Survivorship frame: base rates include the failures the question's frame selects away. Counterfactual suppression: the outside view surfaces the 'what if this fails?' that the inside view suppresses.
